question.text: A long straight wire with a circular cross-section having radius <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>R</mi></math>, is carrying a steady current <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>I</mi></math>. The current <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>I</mi></math> is uniformly distributed across this cross-section. Then the variation of magnetic field due to current <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>I</mi></math> with distance <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>r</mi><mfenced><mrow><mi>r</mi><mo><</mo><mi>R</mi></mrow></mfenced></math> from its centre will be

solution.text:
Using Ampere's law and noting that the steady current is uniformly distributed over the cross-section of the cylindrical wire.

B=μ0Ir2πR2,   r≤Rμ0I2πr,   r>R

Thus, magnetic field B∝r from the centre for r<R.
